title: Files, Errors and Modules
subtitle: Work with files, handle errors and organize Python programs into modules.
description: Learn file operations, exceptions, try/except, imports and basic program organization using reusable modules.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand Files, Errors and Modules

Welcome to Lesson 8: Files, Errors and Modules. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Files, Errors and Modules”. The goal is to work with files, handle errors and organize Python programs into modules.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Errors are part of normal software work: users can enter unexpected values, files may be missing, and external services may fail. Reliable code detects failures at a useful boundary and communicates what happened without pretending the operation succeeded.

blocks.question: A catch/except block is empty. What is the main danger?
options: The code becomes easier to diagnose.
It automatically retries safely.
It guarantees correct data.
It can hide real failures and make the program appear successful.
blocks.explanation: Silently swallowing errors obscures the cause and can lead to corrupted or incomplete results.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Silently swallowing errors obscures the cause and can lead to corrupted or incomplete results.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Silently swallowing errors obscures the cause and can lead to corrupted or incomplete results.

blocks.question: A database query receives user-provided text. Which safeguard is strongest?
options: Build the query by concatenating the text into SQL.
Remove all error messages.
Use parameterized queries and validate the expected data.
Trust the browser because it has a form.
blocks.explanation: Parameters keep user values separate from executable SQL syntax.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Parameters keep user values separate from executable SQL syntax.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Parameters keep user values separate from executable SQL syntax.

blocks.text: Validate data before using it, and catch only failures you can handle meaningfully. Empty catch blocks hide defects; broad recovery can turn a visible problem into silently corrupted data.

blocks.question: A function can return either a result or a failure. What should callers do?
options: Inspect and handle the documented success/error result.
Assume failure means success.
Discard the return value in every case.
Repeat the request infinitely.
blocks.explanation: Callers need to respond to the success or failure contract explicitly.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Callers need to respond to the success or failure contract explicitly.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Callers need to respond to the success or failure contract explicitly.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning

Keep responsibilities separate. A function that reads a file, validates records, computes results, and prints a report is difficult to test; small steps let you isolate a failure and reuse the successful parts.

blocks.question: A file may not exist when a user starts the app. What is the best approach?
options: Assume the file always exists.
Catch every possible error and ignore it.
Check/open the file safely and report a useful recoverable error.
Pretend an empty file is always correct.
blocks.explanation: External resources can fail; communicate the problem and recover only where recovery is appropriate.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. External resources can fail; communicate the problem and recover only where recovery is appropriate.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. External resources can fail; communicate the problem and recover only where recovery is appropriate.

blocks.question: A numeric form field contains “abc”. What should happen?
options: Convert it silently to a meaningful value without a rule.
Parse and validate it, then show a clear error if it is invalid.
Use the string in arithmetic.
Delete the user’s whole account.
blocks.explanation: Parsing and validation protect calculations from malformed input.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Parsing and validation protect calculations from malformed input.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Parsing and validation protect calculations from malformed input.
